topic: What trade-offs exist between reflector aperture size and feed element redundancy in robust antenna design?
consensus_response: In robust antenna design for satellite communications, increasing reflector aperture size enhances directivity but increases the risk of pattern degradation due to feed element failures. Defocused reflectors can mitigate this by overlapping patterns, improving robustness against single-element impact. Phased arrays offer improved robustness through inherent redundancy but increase complexity and potential phase errors. Advanced materials and manufacturing techniques can reduce losses associated with defocused reflectors, enabling larger apertures without compromising structural integrity.
